explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/911: with R̂(G) the size Ramsey number, is there a function f with f(x)/x → ∞ such that, for all large C, any graph G with n vertices and e ≥ Cn edges has R̂(G) > f(C)·e? The Lean statement: ∃ f : ℝ → ℝ with f(x)/x → ∞ along atTop and ∃ C₀ such that for all C ≥ C₀, all n > 0 and all graphs G on Fin n with C·n ≤ e(G), f(C)·e(G) < sizeRamsey G G, where sizeRamsey G G is the least number of edges of a graph F every red/blue edge-colouring of which contains a monochromatic copy of G (diagonal case). The quantifier order (f first, then large C) matches, and the n > 0 hypothesis only removes the empty graph. Faithful.
